sections.title: Evaluation scope
sections.markdown: This is a focused assessment of SAP ABAP Development Tools MCP, not a new attempt to establish whether agent-assisted SAP development can work end to end. Broader engineering workflows may combine models, coding agents, VS Code, SAP development tools and human approval. We evaluated what the MCP interface contributes, what was executed and what remains dependent on other components.

sections.title: What was evaluated
sections.markdown: In a trial ABAP environment, the connected ADT MCP Server exposed 20 tools. A RAP student-management scenario generated 14 related repository artifacts. Activation tools, ATC runs, service discovery and ABAP Unit were exercised. SAP describes the ADT MCP Server as experimental and not intended for productive use.

sections.title: RAP validation and ABAP Unit
sections.markdown:
The final test implementation contained three methods for a valid status, missing name and invalid status. They exercised the RAP business-object save sequence using `MODIFY ENTITIES` and `COMMIT ENTITIES` with an OSQL test double; the MCP runner reported an overall PASS. The test result omitted a per-method count, so the three cases are established from the final editor-agent source excerpt.

Earlier failures were traced to RAP transactional-buffer leakage across tests. A `ROLLBACK ENTITIES` call in test setup provided isolation. This diagnosis is supported by the packaged test history, not by a fresh direct SAP repository readback from the reviewer.

sections.title: ATC and tool results
sections.markdown:
The final ATC worklist reported five open priority-2/priority-3 findings, mainly message-literal and test-code SELECT hygiene issues. These were not waived or presented as an ATC-clean result.

| Tool assessment | Count |
| --- | ---: |
| PASS | 13 |
| PASS with limitation | 2 |
| Permission blocked | 2 |
| Prerequisite unavailable | 2 |
| Not tested by owner decision | 1 |

The deterministic quickfix tool produced a null-pointer error when invoked on an empty ATC worklist. On a nonempty worklist without an applicable fix, it returned an empty, non-error result. No actual deterministic quickfix application was demonstrated. Permission blocks were respected rather than overridden.

sections.title: Service and source boundaries
sections.markdown:
The OData V4 service was reported published and its entity metadata retrieved. No HTTP runtime functional request was executed, so OData-level business behavior was not established.

Custom ABAP source was handled through a compatible VS Code SAP developer-agent editing path, rather than a general-purpose MCP source-write tool. The editor-agent-provided source and MCP test results support the reported lifecycle; an independent live source readback was not available to the reviewer.

sections.title: Architectural conclusion
sections.markdown:
ADT MCP is a typed tool interface within a broader agent-assisted workflow. Its value is in exposing controlled SAP operations. It does not replace the coding agent, IDE, SAP authorizations, executable tests or governance.

The exercise demonstrates a useful development-tool workflow and candid limitations; it is not a production-readiness assessment, a productivity benchmark, or an all-tools-PASS claim.

claims.claim: Earlier integrated engineering work is separate context, not fresh KS01 execution evidence.
claims.limitation: Prior CAPELLA/Synapse work not counted in current MCP tool receipts

claims.claim: The live ADT MCP server exposed 20 tools during the new trial assessment.
claims.limitation: No server-build metadata or SAP SID obtained

claims.claim: A RAP generator produced responses for 14 repository artifacts.
claims.limitation: Repository inventory and activation not independently read back for all artifacts

claims.claim: The final ABAP Unit source excerpt has three RAP EML save-sequence tests; MCP runner reported overall PASS.
claims.limitation: No result-method count; final live source not independently re-read by GPT

claims.claim: ATC returned five remaining P2/P3 static analysis findings.
claims.limitation: Curated receipt, not raw SAP JSON; not an ATC clean result

claims.claim: 20-tool statuses: 13 PASS, 2 limited, 2 blocked by permissions, 2 prerequisite-unavailable, 1 not tested.
claims.limitation: The two limited tools did not demonstrate positive paths for all conditions

claims.claim: Deterministic quickfix invoked against an empty worklist reported a null-pointer error.
claims.limitation: No successful eligible quickfix application demonstrated

claims.claim: V4 service published and discoverable through MCP, without an OData HTTP functional test.
claims.limitation: OData business validation through HTTP not tested

claims.claim: Source edits were conducted via SAP developer agent in VS Code, not via a generic MCP source-write tool.
claims.limitation: No independent live final-source readback by GPT or Claude

claims.claim: ADT MCP Server is described by SAP as experimental and not for productive use.
claims.limitation: Trial research is not production certification
